headline: ROGUE learns to run away
lede: The dungeon's creatures stopped marching in lockstep: fast races now double-step, trolls hesitate, wounded monsters flee for good — and a snake that bites you turns tail. Slot a shipped the 1980 mobility laws to /retrogames/rogue.

notes.text: Per-monster energy clocks: kestrels, bats, centaurs, leprechauns and jabberwocks act 1.5x, trolls and medusae 0.75x — measured in the harness at 6 and 3 actions per 4 hero turns, not just declared in a table.
The flee law: a wounded creature that sees you (hp at or below a quarter of its own max) breaks off and runs, never to turn brave again — unless you corner it, then it bites.

The snake has its own 1980 law: once it bites you it flees for good. Proof went to real Chrome — roguedrive scans seeds, replays the exact key route, and lands on a byte-identical state hash before watching the snake run.
Careful in the halls: roguecheck 116/116, drive 18/18, watchcheck 318/318 — zero new generation RNG, so every old seed world still generates bit-identical; only the monsters grew up.

look.text: Wound something and watch it break for the door
